plan: My value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk not winning when I should. If I bid more, I might pay more than my value if I win. The worst-case scenario with a $25 bid is paying slightly less than $25 if I win, which preserves my potential profit. Other bidders' values are unknown, so a true-value bid is most robust.

My value is $31. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. The worst case is paying close to my value, but bidding $31 ensures I only win if the prize is genuinely worth more than the second-highest bid. This maximizes my expected profit.

My private value is $9. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is typically to bid close to my true value. Since the prize is won by highest bidder but paid only the second-highest price, I want to maximize potential profit. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk significant loss. A bid around $10-$11 seems strategic - close to my value but with upside potential.
